video_title: Jason Sudeikis Almost Played Junior College Ball Against Stephen Jackson

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Sudeikis on his junior college basketball experience at Fort Scott
quotes.excerpt: Fort Scott was the one me and two dudes from my high school team in class we went

text_blocks.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
text_blocks.text: I went to Fort Scott Community College, which was the Jayhawk Conference West. All of them came after me after senior year, like Barton County, Butler, Hutch. Fort Scott was the one me and two dudes from my high school team in class we went down there an hour and a half south, you know, one highway. And I was ineligible my second semester. I didn't go to a lick of class.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: That's what junior college is for, people that didn't take high school serious. What made you think you were going to get it in a couple months?

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Sudeikis recalls watching Ruben Patterson play in junior college
quotes.excerpt: I remember watching we played against Independence Community College against Ruben Patterson, he had 40 points
quotes.quote: I remember watching we played against Independence Community College against Ruben Patterson, he had 40 points, 38 and more dunks. I was in like a tie and jeans looking like I was in Boys to Men or something and I had like a denim shirt I got from Structure and I'm just sitting there on the end of the bench just watching this guy going to town on us. I was like, well, I'm going to keep an eye on him.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Sudeikis on Tay Officer's talent and eligibility issues
quotes.excerpt: He was the guy that not only lovely, he was incredible and he was just like happy
quotes.quote: We had one dude that was straight up the best, Tay Officer. He played, he came up through the whole Kansas City, you know, AAU, Myron Piggie world. He was the guy that not only lovely, he was incredible and he was just like happy and this but he got ineligible freshman year and he couldn't play, but we would go head to head and he was so much better than me, but he liked me because I was like flashy and he called me white magic. I was like, I'll take it.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Sudeikis discusses the talent of Jaron Rush
quotes.excerpt: Jaron Rush played, yeah, Jaron was incredible. I knew him as an eighth grader.
quotes.quote: Jaron Rush played, yeah, Jaron was incredible. I knew him as an eighth grader. He was good friends with my ex-brother-in-law, my sister and her boyfriend way back when and then eventually husband. They were like, we all played under the Children's Mercy Hospital, like Tom Grant who was the one that funded all that. We had 17 unders, 16, 15, so I was in 15 under and 16 under those two years and so Jaron would have been 12 and 13 under. I mean, him and his brother, incredible.

quotes.speaker: Matt Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Matt Barnes and Jason Sudeikis discuss the careers of the Rush brothers
quotes.excerpt: Kareem, he played for the Lakers, then Brandon played for, won a championship with the Warriors

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: That's Kareem, he played for the Lakers, then Brandon played for, won a championship with the Warriors, but Jaron never made it to the league, but he was in me and Ray's class at UCLA, but he was the best one out of all of us.

text_blocks.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
text_blocks.text: Supposed to go to KU. Coming out here was a lot, but I think KU would have been a lot. He should have went somewhere else. I think LA was bad for him, especially with all the little habits he had, so it was just like, I don't know him like that because by that point I'd lost touch with him.
